newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR says no decision on asset sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR says no decision on asset sales.

text.p: Building materials, aluminium and sugar group CSR Ltd said on Wednesday it had not reached a decision yet on the outcome of a review of its operations as part of a process to help boost the group's performance.

CSR said last May it would form a taskforce to look at ways of improving the return on its assets. The Sydney Morning Herald said on Wednesday that CSR was poised to raise about A$1 billion from a shake-up of its local timber and U.S. businesses.
"We are in the middle of a process and there are a whole host of outcomes," company secretary Peter Abraham told Reuters. "It may end up that we sell nothing; it may be we do sell."
"If we sold every business then presumably it would be a lot more than that (A$1.0 billion). Whether we sell them or not is not something that has been decided either," Abraham said.

"It is all a question of looking at these businesses and looking at the best options for either improving them restructuring them joint venturing them and determing at the end of the day what the best alternatives are," he said.
He said brokers CS First Boston and management consultants McKinsey and Co were helping CSR with its restructure review.
In November, CSR said it expected second half earnings for the 1996/97 (April/March) year to be lower than a year earlier.
The expected lower 1996/97 year result would be the second successive year CSR would report an annual profit fall.
The company has blamed the weak Australian building market for its profit woes.
At 11.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), CSR shares were six cents up at A$4.35.
